messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty ALERT -> P0: VentureBridge prod VPC auth failures detected (token introspection & mTLS fail). Started 02:13 UTC. Paging on-call.

ashley (oncall): ACK. I’m on it, grabbing context. Which tenant is hit?

kevin (eng-sre): Looks like a single enterprise tenant: venture-bridge-prod (dedicated VPC + private auth bridge). Errors: TLS handshake aborted / x509: certificate signed by unknown authority in auth-proxy logs.

lina (infra): Confirming. I can see backend auth-proxy returning 400 on introspect requests. Istio mutual-tls handshake failing upstream.

kevin (eng-sre): Pasting relevant snippet from auth-proxy logs:
```
2026-03-15T02:14:02Z auth-proxy[main] ERROR handshake failed: remote error: tls: bad certificate
2026-03-15T02:14:02Z auth-proxy[main] DEBUG introspect request failed: 401 - kid not found: KID 0x7a3b
```

ashley (oncall): Kid not found + TLS bad cert suggests ephemeral client cert expired or rotation never completed. Any recent rotation jobs for venture-bridge?

sam (platform): There was a scheduled ephemeral cert rotation job yesterday 23:00 UTC for that tenant. Cron job reported success but I see S3 upload step returned 403 for the new cert artifact — might be permission regression on the customer bucket.

kevin (eng-sre): If the auth bridge doesn't have the new client cert, it will present the old/expired cert -> mTLS fail. Two mitigation paths: 1) quick rollback: disable tenant-enforced client cert validation for that tenant (require_client_cert=false) to restore traffic while we re-provision certs; 2) re-run rotate flow but push certs to the dedicated keystore directly and restart auth-proxy. Option 1 has security implications; need account approval.

david (acct-mgr): I’m on standby to notify VentureBridge. If we recommend disabling client cert enforcement temporarily, they need to accept the risk. I'll call them now.

ashley (oncall): Quick check — can we fail traffic to a compatible dedicated pool that accepts token-based auth (no mTLS) without touching tenant config? i.e., route to fallback pool?

lina (infra): We have a routing rule that can send traffic for that tenant to the regional fallback pool (eu-west-1-dedicated-fallback). That pool is compatible but capacity is limited. We can shift a percentage to fallback as a partial mitigation.

kevin (eng-sre): Do that immediately as a safety valve. Lina — can you flip the routing weight to 70% fallback, 30% primary? That should let most traffic through and reduce customer impact while we fix certs.

lina (infra): On it. Running command:
```bash
redwood route update --tenant venture-bridge-prod --weights primary=30,fallback=70 --region eu-west-1
```

lina (infra): Done. Monitoring latency and errors. Metrics look better in the last 30s (5xx down ~70%).

kevin (eng-sre): Good. Now for the upstream fix: I’ll re-run the cert-rotation with manual S3 credentials — bypass the broken cron path and push the cert to the tenant keystore. Steps: 1) generate new client certs signed by customer CA (using stored CSR), 2) upload to keystore, 3) restart auth-proxy. I’ll do step 1 and 2; Lina can restart proxies.

ashley (oncall): Assigning tasks: kevin -> generate & upload certs; lina -> restart auth-proxy once uploaded; david -> confirm customer notification/approval if we need to disable verify (not yet needed). I’ll coordinate.

kevin (eng-sre): Generating cert now. Command used:
```bash
openssl x509 -req -in venture-bridge.csr -CA customer-root.pem -CAkey customer-root.key -days 7 -sha256 -out client.pem -extensions usr_cert
```
Uploading to keystore with admin API:
```bash
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -F "keystore=@client.pem" https://admin.internal/tenants/venture-bridge/keystore
```
Upload returned 200.

lina (infra): Received artifact, restarting auth-proxy pods for tenant bridge (graceful):
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deploy/venture-bridge-auth-proxy -n tenant-venture-bridge --grace-period=30
```
Restart in progress.

ops-bot: Deployment rollout status: 2/2 updated, 2/2 available.

kevin (eng-sre): Post-restart checks: TLS handshake now OK, introspection returning 200. Sample log:
```
2026-03-15T02:24:11Z auth-proxy[main] INFO handshake complete: client CN=venture-proxy-ephemeral
2026-03-15T02:24:12Z auth-proxy[main] INFO introspect success: token valid, tenant venture-bridge-prod
```

ashley (oncall): Nice work. Lina — revert routing weights back to primary=100, fallback=0 once you confirm stability for 5 minutes.

lina (infra): Reverting now.

lina (infra): Route update done. Errors back to baseline. No 5xx seen in last 3m.

david (acct-mgr): I spoke to VentureBridge legal/ops. They approved the emergency rotation we performed (manual upload) but want a postmortem and assurance this won't recur. They asked we avoid disabling auth controls in future.

kevin (eng-sre): Short RCA draft: automated rotation job succeeded through CSR generation, but S3 upload step failed due to an IAM policy change on the customer bucket that removed the service account's PutObject permission. The cron job interpreted the 403 as success (bug in error handling) and didn't rollback. Manual rotation and keystore push restored service. Action items: 1) Fix cron job error handling and alert on S3 non-2xx, 2) add S3 write check in pre-rotation step, 3) add canary rotation for enterprise tenants before global job runs, 4) automate failover routing runbook.

ashley (oncall): Creating incident ticket INC-312345 in tracker, assigning to eng-sre and infra. Also scheduling a post-incident review with VentureBridge this week.

david (acct-mgr): Customer follow-up: I'll send a brief timeline and plan for mitigation + long-term remediation.

kevin (eng-sre): Leaving one follow-up: recommend rotating the short-lived certs to 14h TTL and schedule stager reupload probes.

ashley (oncall): Thanks everyone. Marking incident as resolved in PagerDuty. Closing thread once incident ticket created.

incident-bot: PagerDuty RESOLVE -> P0: VentureBridge prod VPC auth failures resolved at 02:35 UTC. Refer INC-312345 for notes and follow-ups.
